transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-20
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Sierra Solutions - Head Infra), Claire Gomez (Sierra - Security PM), Tom Lee (Sierra - Eng Lead)

Summary section (auto-gen):
Redwood presented data handling controls — emphasis on toggles for request storage, automatic PII redaction, and policy-driven retention. Customer wanted confirmation around e-discovery/legal hold and whether ephemeral logs can be exported before deletion.

Topics covered: Console toggles, API-level flags, redaction rule editor, KMS-backed S3 exports, audit logs, Optimize recommendations.

--- Transcript body (timestamps are approximate and transcription imperfect) ---
00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through the retention and redaction settings in the Console and show equivalent API calls, and then Ethan will demo some of the redaction rules live, so feel free to interrupt with questions
00:12 Ravi: yeah thanks, Maya. quick context — we're evaluating for customer-facing chat, dealing with PII and PCI-ish data, compliance team will need to sign off, so big questions are can we turn off storage per-route and do we get auditable proofs when data is redacted
00:28 Maya: great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Ethan — do you want to start in Console?
00:33 Ethan: sure. so in Console you have a Request Storage setting at the route level. right now it's set to Persist by default, you can flip to Ephemeral and that will not write request bodies to long-term request storage. small caveat: short-lived caches like K-V cache are still there for inference performance but encrypted in memory. (mutter) K V cache… sometimes the transcript says K V cache
00:55 Claire: sorry can I interrupt, when you say ephemeral — what's the retention window? is ephemeral immediate deletion or more like 24 hours?
01:02 Ethan: good call. Ephemeral means we keep the request for up to 1 hour for debugging and tracing, then delete. You can also set a custom retention in Console — 0 minutes (meaning immediate shuffle) up to 90 days for persisted logs. so ephemeral equals short-term, persist equals configured retention window.
01:19 Tom: and what's the export story? if legal asks for data for a given user within the hour can we export before it's removed?
01:25 Ethan: yes, the audit + export tool will let you run an export job. if ephemeral storage is on, you have that 1-hour window to pull it out; after deletion it's gone unless you configured an archive export ahead of time to an S3 bucket. We support KMS-backed buckets so keys are customer-managed.
01:41 Claire: So KMS — is that our KMS or Redwood's? we need customer-managed keys.
01:45 Maya: you can provide a CMK in AWS KMS or equivalent HSM; Redwood's export will use customer-managed keys for S3 writes. we also produce audit logs for key usage.
01:53 Ravi: ok good. next, redaction — automatic PII detection, how reliable is that?
01:58 Ethan: we have an auto PII detector that flags things like SSNs, credit card numbers, emails, phone numbers. it's ML-based with named entity heuristics and regex fallbacks. important to note: auto-detection is a best-effort; for regulated flows we recommend adding custom regex masks to catch company-specific tokens.
02:18 Tom: what's the precedence? if auto-detect and a custom regex both match do we get double-mask or single mask?
02:23 Ethan: precedence is: explicit allowlist/denylist rules, then custom regex masks, then auto-detect. we apply the first matching mask rule. we'll show the editor in a sec.
02:30 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
02:38 Ethan: ok switching to the Console now — this is the Route settings page. under Data handling you see Request Storage, Redaction Rules, and Audit retention. I'll create a sample rule: regex "(?i)acct\s*#?\d{4,}" to catch nonstandard account IDs, apply mask type = partial-mask, and scope = request.body.
02:59 Claire: can those rules be applied per-route or globally?
03:04 Ethan: both. rules can be scoped at the org, project, or route level. global rules inherit down and can be overridden at route level.
03:12 Maya: quick note on API — anything you do in Console has a corresponding API call so infra teams can automate. for example the route patch API accepts a request_storage field with values ["persist","ephemeral","none"] and a redaction_rules array (we'll paste examples).
03:28 Ravi: can you show the exact API body? that's what our infra team needs to review.
03:33 Ethan: yeah here — POST /v1/routes/:id/settings { "request_storage": "ephemeral", "redaction_rules": [{"name":"acct-mask","pattern":"(?i)acct\\s*#?\\d{4,}", "mask_type":"partial"}], "retention_days": 1 } — this is simplified but we'll send the SDK example.
03:56 Tom: does changing to ephemeral impact latency? we've seen other vendors add overhead when masking on the fly.
04:02 Ethan: great question. masking is applied asynchronously in our pipeline for writes. inference path uses in-memory caches and mask-less tokens are not delayed — we do streaming redaction for responses when needed, but overall overhead is minimal ~10-20ms depending on rule complexity. our runtime supports optimized kernels and batched masking.
04:25 Claire: what about audit logs? we need a separation between request content and audit metadata — e.g., who accessed what and when.
04:31 Maya: audit logs are separate — they contain metadata (route, user, token id, timestamp, operation). content is in request storage. audit logs are write-once and can be forwarded to customers' SIEM via webhook or exported to S3.
04:44 Ravi: legal hold scenario: if we have to preserve certain conversations for litigation, can we override retention on specific objects?
04:51 Ethan: yes — we support pinning or legal hold at the object level via the API. the hold prevents deletion regardless of route-level retention until the hold is removed. it's part of the export+archive flow.
05:05 Claire: is legal hold logged? we need to show tamper-proof evidence that hold was applied and by whom.
05:11 Maya: every hold operation is recorded in the audit log with actor and timestamp. audit logs themselves are immutable and available for export.
05:18 Ravi: okay, show us the redaction editor live please.
05:22 Ethan: switching — (typing) here's the redaction UI. you can test rules against sample payloads in the editor. I'm pasting a sample chat, see how the regex masks the account numbers and the auto-detector flags an SSN and masks it. note: the tester simulates the runtime but actual throughput may differ.
05:40 Ethan: (sigh) small transcript quirk — sometimes the demo dashboard says "retention, re-tent ion" — ignore that.
05:48 Tom: can we chain masks? for example mask entire message if contains PCI and otherwise do partial?
05:53 Ethan: yes you can have conditional rules; the rule engine supports if-then style ordering. examples: if contains PCI token then mask full_message else apply partial masks. we'll provide sample policy templates.
06:06 Claire: do we support redaction in embeddings pipelines? we use embeddings for search and can't store sensitive vectors.
06:12 Ethan: embeddings can be configured to never persist or to be salted/hashed before storage. Optimize can also flag high-risk tokens to avoid embedding them or to remove PII before vectorization.
06:23 Ravi: how does Optimize tie in? we've seen your docs mention suggestions.
06:27 Maya: Optimize scans route metrics and will propose toggles — e.g., suggest ephemeral storage for dev routes, or recommend masking patterns if token leakage detected. it's advisory and you can accept changes via API or Console.
06:37 Tom: another question — how granular is RBAC? can we restrict export capability to a small group?
06:43 Maya: yes RBAC integrates with SSO/SAML and supports roles: Admin, Auditor, Operator, Viewer. export and legal-hold require Admin or designated Operator role. we can map to your IdP groups.
06:54 Claire: we use Okta; is SAML supported or only OIDC?
06:58 Maya: both. we support SAML, OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning.
07:05 Ravi: there may be a need to run Redwood Private in our VPC — in that case is request storage still managed by us?
07:12 Ethan: with Private deployment you manage the storage endpoints and keys — Redwood control plane can be deployed into your VPC and logs never leave your network unless you opt-in for exports. encryption and KMS are customer-managed.
07:23 Tom: great. demo question: what happens if a redaction rule has a false positive? we need ability to unmask for troubleshooting but restrict who can do that.
07:31 Ethan: we support a Just-In-Time reveal flow: a user with Approve Unmask permission can request an unmask, which creates a one-time access token, recorded in audit logs, and the data is revealed for a predefined short window. every reveal is audited.
07:44 Claire: that helps. okay, what's the SLA for deletion? if retention says 7 days, is deletion guaranteed at exactly 7 days or eventual?
07:52 Ethan: deletion is guaranteed by policy — our jobs run with strong consistency; for enterprise contracts we provide a deletion certificate showing job completion time.
08:02 Maya: quick pause — any other compliance check questions?
08:06 Claire: do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001?
08:09 Maya: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001, plus pen test reports we can share under NDA.
08:16 Ravi: can you show how to set up a route for ephemeral requests via API, we want the curl form please.
08:22 Ethan: sure — curl -X PATCH "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/123/settings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"request_storage":"ephemeral","retention_days":0,"redaction_rules":[{"name":"email-mask","pattern":"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}","mask_type":"partial"}]}'
08:46 Tom: thanks. can the curl be tied into terraform or do you have a provider?
08:50 Maya: we have a Terraform provider and raw API examples; we'll link both.
08:55 Claire: last question on data residency — if we run in region eu-west-1 does Redwood keep data in region?
09:00 Maya: yes — for hosted deployments we can pin region and the storage and compute will stay in that region, and for Private it's your infra.
09:07 Ravi: ok good. any hidden gotchas we should know about when flipping storage off for production?
09:13 Ethan: the main one is debugging/traceability — ephemeral removes long-term request visibility so if you need postmortem of user issues you'll want a short retention window or selective persisting for certain routes. also some observability integrations rely on request bodies to surface errors — we have metadata-based traces to help mitigate.
09:33 Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
09:40 Maya: wrap up recap: we showed Console toggles and API examples, redaction editor and test harness, KMS-backed exports, legal hold flow, and RBAC + SSO mapping. Next we'll send the sample policy JSON, Terraform snippets, and SOC/ISO artifacts.
09:58 Ravi: thanks everyone, sounds good. we'll pick a pilot scope — likely chat support routes only, enable ephemeral for dev, 7-day retention for prod, and test a 14-day legal hold flow.
10:12 Claire: please include example regexes for our legacy account tokens.
10:16 Maya: will do. Thanks all for your time.

End of transcript.
